searchText: Should miners be allowed to *not* accept the full gas_premium? The python code I have asserts that the miner received the full gas premium, but in theory if a miner wanted to craft a lock where they didn't extract the full premium I don't see a strong reason that should result in an invalid block. I do think that the logic for "miners **MUST** receive the calculated `premium_per_gas`" is simpler for validation, so if no one has a strong opinion that miners should be able to *reject* the premium then I would prefer to keep the logic such that it requires miners to take the premium. I would still like to rename (colloquially) `gas_premium` to `maximum_miner_bribe`. Not a consensus change, though I do think there is value in all of the clients using shared terminology which is why I bring it up here. I think `maximum_miner_bribe` is a bit more clear to users, and I suspect that the variable names that clients use will likely end up being what end-users use colloquially, so picking something easy for end-users to understand is valuable IMO. To anyone not subscribed to the GitHub issue, I have updated my PR to include a rewrite of the abstract, to see if that addresses the concerns some people have expressed over there not being a good plain English description of the new fee system. Definitely open to feedback, though I intentionally am leaving the specific formulas for the specification as I don't think people should be trying to implement from the abstract. <@!376568077950910466> Did you indicate that currently Geth/Besu truncate (round to 0) rather than round to negative infinity when doing integer division? Is this standard across clients, or is this the first time that clients have had to divide a negative before? You have convinced me, by the way, to include a definition for `//`, mainly because searching the internet for operators is a serious PITA. In the process of doing that, I realized that maybe I misunderstood what rounding mechanism you all agreed on and wanted to make sure I define it correctly (and potentially fix the python if Python's `//` doesn't do the right thing for consensus. > <@!203220829473996800> iirc Celo also has an EIP 1559 implementation. always was curious to check how it's going, I should spin up a node and get the data <@!486501030046203915> Yes, they were engaging Gauntlet at the same time we were... FWIW. What's going on on 28 August?#EIP1559 > I do think that the logic for "miners **MUST** receive the calculated `premium_per_gas`" is simpler for validation, so if no one has a strong opinion that miners should be able to *reject* the premium then I would prefer to keep the logic such that it requires miners to take the premium. <@!301186049323958275> Let's minimize games and force miners to take it, please and thank you. <@740821105337434164> https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/197
